<thought>Based on the high‑intensity peak at m/z 262.099 Da from the ESI‑MS spectrum, the most plausible ion is an [M + NH₄]⁺ adduct. Subtracting the mass of NH₄⁺ (18.0338 Da) gives a neutral molecular mass of ≈ 244.07 Da. The formula C₁₄H₁₂O₄ matches this mass (exact monoisotopic mass = 244.0736 Da) within typical high‑resolution MS error, and contains only C, H, and O as required. Therefore the molecular formula of the sample is C₁₄H₁₂O₄. </thought>
<final_answer>C14H12O4</final_answer>
